name: Global Water Resources
headline: A small Arizona water and wastewater utility protected by exclusive service certificates.
what_short: Regulated Arizona water and wastewater utility
what_it_does: Global Water Resources runs 39 water, wastewater and recycled-water systems in Arizona, serving 68,577 active connections. All of its revenue ($55.8 million in 2025) is regulated by the Arizona Corporation Commission, and 87.3% of its connections are in one service area.
why_it_passed: It holds an exclusive certificate to serve its territory, and no rival would pay to duplicate the pipes.
All revenue is regulated, so the next ten years of its business are easy to picture.
It found and disclosed on its own a rate-base error carried for fourteen years, which went against its own revenue, so honesty was not in doubt.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what a utility may earn, so the price is far above what that capped return justifies. At $7.74 a share the price is above the top of the analysis's value range, and the company earned only about 4% on its capital against an allowed return more than twice that.
watch: The regulator's staff once recommended a decrease and its largest rate case was withdrawn, so the regulatory climate is an open risk.
Cities have twice taken over a franchise by condemnation.
Management's ability was weighed against, and it has about $127 million of net debt and refundable advances of $155.7 million from builders.
